correction.summary: HIT: Germany / Bavaria / Munich confirmed, and the analyst even landed in Schwabing-West with only 2.7 km error. The German red 'A' Apotheke emblem, RSA red/white barrier boards with amber blinkers, and an ERDINGER WEISSBRÄU firewall mural excluded Austria and Switzerland and fixed Upper Bavaria; the grassed double-track tram reservation on a long straight radial avenue with kilometre-long 5-6 storey rendered perimeter blocks pinned Munich over Nuremberg/Augsburg. discriminators.title: Pharmacy emblem separates Germany from Austria and Switzerland
discriminators.body: In Germany a pharmacy shows a red 'APOTHEKE' sign with the stylized red 'A' containing a vessel and snake. In Austria you would instead see a green-and-white cross with serpent-and-bowl and often 'Apotheke zum …' naming; in Switzerland a plain green cross with 'Apotheke/Pharmacie'. Treat the red A as near-conclusive for Germany.

discriminators.title: German RSA roadworks boards vs Austrian/Swiss site furniture
discriminators.body: In Germany construction zones use red/white diagonally striped rectangular barrier boards on orange plastic bases with small amber flashing lamps, plus blue-and-white site container fences. In Austria you would more often see red/white striped tubular barriers with reflective panels and yellow warning beacons of a different shape; Switzerland uses orange-red barriers with black-yellow chevrons. Roadworks kit is a fast DACH discriminator.

discriminators.title: Munich green tram reservations vs Vienna paved tram track
discriminators.body: In Munich radial avenues the tram runs on a long grassed, kerbed reservation in the median with catenary hung on span wires. In Vienna, which looks similarly Gründerzeit, trams usually share the asphalt carriageway or run on paved track, and catenary is carried on ornate wall rosettes with far more overhead crossing wires. Grass track over kilometres plus rendered Bavarian blocks points to Munich.

discriminators.title: Bavarian brewery firewall murals localise the state
discriminators.body: In Upper Bavaria firewall gables carry painted wheat-beer roundels (Erdinger, Paulaner, Augustiner). In Rhineland or Saxony you would instead see Kölsch, Bitburger or Radeberger branding, and the surrounding facades would be clinker brick rather than ochre stucco. Brewery advertising is a reliable federal-state cue.

discriminators.title: Munich vs Nuremberg/Augsburg tram-city street proportions
discriminators.body: In Munich the tram corridors are very wide radials flanked by continuous 5-6 storey rendered blocks with retail plinths and heavy scaffolded refurbishment. In Nuremberg you would instead see narrower streets with red sandstone and postwar reconstruction detail, and in Augsburg a much smaller-scale 3-4 storey centre. Street width plus block height settles the Bavarian tram city.
